“The locus of ethical problems lies not in the consciousness of the…” — Watsuji Tetsuro (Rinrigaku: Ethics in Japan, trans. Yamamoto…)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Rinrigaku: Ethics in Japan, trans. Yamamoto & Carter, p. 10. Theme: ethics.

Quotes / Watsuji Tetsuro / Q0657

English

The locus of ethical problems lies not in the consciousness of the isolated individual, but precisely in the in-betweenness of person and person.
Thinker Watsuji Tetsuro
School Kyoto School
Source Rinrigaku: Ethics in Japan, trans. Yamamoto & Carter, p. 10
Theme Ethics

About Watsuji Tetsuro

Watsuji Tetsurō (1889–1960) was a Japanese ethicist associated with Kyoto intellectual life who criticized Heidegger for privileging temporality and the isolated individual. Climate and Culture (Fūdo) and the multi-volume Rinrigaku relocate ethics in betweenness (aidagara) and in the spatial-climatic milieu that shapes persons.

How to read this passage

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably Kwame Anthony Appiah and Simone de Beauvoir), ethics is framed through Africana Philosophy and Existentialism. Some passages define ethics; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language. This passage enters that discussion through ethics, relation.
